messages:
Alex P: Quick context — large enterprise customer asked for a migration path from org-level API keys to per-project delegated keys + rotation without breaking existing integrations. They also want clear audit logs and a way to bind keys to specific model routes (chat vs embeddings).

Maria (PM): Thanks Alex. Can we outline the minimal viable surface for launch vs stretch? Also need acceptance criteria we can show sales.

Dave R: Rough engineering constraints: runtime needs to accept either org key or project key. If we add an `X-Project-ID` header we can avoid modifying existing token format immediately. But long-term we should support canonical project-scoped keys (like `proj_{id}_key`) and deprecate org keys.

Sasha S: Security asks: rotation API + audit trail are non-negotiable for enterprise. We should integrate with KMS/HSM for key wrapping and emit key-use events to audit log (who/when/route). Also specify TTLs for rotated keys and an emergency revoke path.

Alex P: Proposal sketch (v1):
- Support project-scoped API keys (read/write subset of routes) + org-level admin keys.
- Accept `Authorization: Bearer <key>` OR `X-Project-ID`+`Authorization` for phased migration.
- Rotation endpoints: `POST /v1/admin/keys/:id/rotate` (returns new key, old key grace 5m default).
- Telemetry: per-key cost/latency counters + audit events.

Maria (PM): Launch vs stretch?
- Launch (v1): project keys + rotation endpoint + admin UI to create/revoke + docs + 2 pilot customers. Acceptance: rotate w/o 500s, audit entries appear, SDK examples updated.
- Stretch (v2): delegated sub-keys for function/tool-calls, time-limited ephemeral keys, per-route quotas, automatic rotation webhooks.

Dave R: Engineering notes:
- Runtime changes: need fast lookup for key -> project mapping; cache in-memory with TTL to avoid DB hits on every request. That affects prefix/KV cache (we must key cache by canonical project id to avoid leaking cached completions across projects).
- Billing: per-key attribution must be wired into tokens so CostService can report per-project.
- SDK: add helper `RedwoodClient({apiKey, projectId})` that sets header. Backwards-compatible if projectId omitted.

Sasha S: Rotation details to decide:
- Grace period: short grace (e.g. 60s-5m) vs session-based rotation (longer) — customers vary. We should make configurable at org level.
- Replay/forensics: store last 30 days of key use metadata (user agent, route, cost token count). That has storage + retention cost; sales will need to price.

Alex P: Edge cases:
- Function calling/tool invocation: keys must specify allowed external tool scopes, else we risk unauthorized tool use.
- Embeddings & rerank: keys should support scoping to model families for compliance (e.g., restrict to open models).
- Backwards compatibility: allow org keys to be mapped to a default project to avoid breaking customers who hardcode a single key.

Maria (PM): Customer-driven asks to log for prioritization:
- Pilot A: needs per-project keys + rotation + audit (high urgency).
- Pilot B: wants ephemeral session keys for end-user embedding flows (medium).
- Sales N: asks for per-route quotas and per-key billing (low for v1).

Dave R: Estimated effort (very rough):
- Auth MVP (project keys + rotation API + admin UI): 3 sprints (2 engs full-time + 1 infra).
- Billing/telemetry plumbing: 2 sprints (1 eng + 1 infra).
- SDK + docs: 2 weeks.

Sasha S: Launch checklist items for security/compliance:
- KMS integration + key-encryption-at-rest.
- Audit events emitted to SIEM (syslog/forwarder).
- Threat model update + test plan for key compromise scenarios.

Alex P: Can we pick owners and a pilot timeline? I suggest:
- Alex P -> product owner for feature (spec + sales comms).
- Dave R -> eng lead (runtime + SDK)
- Sasha S -> security/compliance owner
- Maria -> acceptance criteria + pilot coordination

build-bot: Deployed staging feature-flag `project-keys` to env:staging at 2026-10-05T18:22:00Z :rocket:

Maria (PM): Next steps: draft PRD based on this thread, prioritize in next planning sync (Thu). If we agree, Dave — can you confirm rough ETA for a canary by end of Q4?

Dave R: I'll scope into sprint planning. Canary by EoQ4 looks feasible if we carve out the infra work first. Will post a breakdown by EOD tomorrow.

Alex P: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone. If you have specific constraints from legal or sales add them here. We'll link the PRD in this thread once David posts breakdown.
